sections.name: GithubHeatmapProps
sections.title: Heatmap input
sections.what: Declares that the component receives a map from date text to completion count.
sections.why: Lets the parent decide which habit data is shown.

sections.name: GithubHeatmap (part 1)
sections.title: Day grid and colors
sections.what: Builds the last 365 days, counts completions for each, groups them into columns of seven, picks a shade from each day's count, and draws each square with a hover label showing the date and count.
sections.why: Makes a year of activity visible as one grid.
sections.watch_out: Date labels use UTC while weekday uses local time, so a day can be off by one near midnight.

sections.name: GithubHeatmap (part 2)
sections.title: Color legend
sections.what: Draws the Less to More Consistency legend under the grid.
sections.watch_out: The legend colors are typed out by hand and must match the grid's color rules if those change.

summary: A grid of 365 small squares, one per day, shaded darker for days with more habit completions.
purpose: Shows consistency over the past year at a glance.
why: Likely reason: to copy the familiar GitHub contribution graph. The code names this style but does not explain the choice.
how: Builds the last 365 days and counts completions for each. Groups the days into columns of seven. Picks a shade for each day from its count. Draws the squares with a hover label and a color legend.
inputs: A map from date text (YYYY-MM-DD) to the number of completions on that day.
risks: Date labels come from UTC time while weekday comes from local time, so a day near midnight can land on the wrong square. The columns are groups of seven, not aligned to weekdays, so the first column may not start on Sunday. The weekday value is calculated but not used.
debug: If a day shows the wrong count, compare its date key with the habit history. If squares look misaligned, check the grouping logic and the local time zone.
